Empirical Research Plan: “How Much Do Individual Managers Matter for Firm Policies and Performance?”

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. IDENTIFICATION STRATEGY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen method: A stacked Difference-in-Differences (DID) / event-study design that exploits manager moves across firms (first used in labor economics by Abowd-Kramarz-Margolis and in finance by Bertrand & Schoar, but here formalised as DID).

Why appropriate
• We observe the same firm before and after the arrival of a new manager (within-firm time variation).  
• We can compare those dynamics to a contemporaneous control group of firms that keep the same manager (cross-sectional variation).  
• Stacking all switches gives many “mini-experiments,” allowing us to flexibly test pre-trends and dynamic post-effects.  
• Two-way (firm × year) FE soak up aggregate shocks and permanent firm heterogeneity; manager FE isolate time-invariant manager talent.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TREATMENT AND CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Unit of observation Firm-year

Treatment variable Treat_it = 1 if firm i is managed by a new manager j starting in fiscal year t0 and t ≥ t0 (t0 = first full fiscal year in office).

Treatment timing / event date Event time = t – t0, where t0 is the first fiscal year in which the incoming manager is officially CEO/President (or equivalent top title). We use a ±5-year symmetric window (−5…+5) for event-study plots; the DID specification keeps all available years.

Control group  
(1) Within-firm pre-period (t < t0) → baseline trend.  
(2) Matched firms that do NOT experience a managerial change in t0 (propensity-score or exact industry-size-year matching) → contemporaneous counterfactual.  

We will “stack” each treated firm-switch and assign a comparison set of firms in the same 3-digit SIC × size decile × calendar year that keep the incumbent manager.

No RDD (no running variable), no IV used for the main specification, but see robustness.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. KEY IDENTIFYING ASSUMPTIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends Absent the new manager, treated firms would have evolved like matched control firms.  
Plausibility: Manager moves are often for idiosyncratic reasons (poaching, retirement of predecessor). We will verify by plotting pre-trends (event-time −5…−1).  

A2. Exogenous timing of moves relative to unobserved shocks A surge in performance or policy is not what makes the board hire a particular “style” manager.  
Plausibility: Less believable for voluntary hires; more believable for forced turnovers or deaths ⇒ we will test heterogeneity (forced vs. voluntary).  

A3. No anticipation / no partial treatment Stakeholders do not change behaviour well in advance of formal appointment.  
Plausibility: There can be leakage; we will include leads of treatment to test.  

A4. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): a manager’s arrival at firm A does not directly change policies at control firms.  
Plausibility: Except perhaps in narrowly defined product-market rivals; we can drop same-industry rivals in sensitivity analyses.  

A5. Common support: treated firms have comparable observables to control firms. Achieved through exact/match restrictions ‑> test via covariate balance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. THREATS TO IDENTIFICATION & MITIGATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1 Selection on unobservable performance trends (“pull” hiring)  
Fix: (i) plot event-study pre-trends; (ii) focus on forced/health turnovers; (iii) include firm-specific linear time trends.  

Threat 2 Manager chooses firms that are about to improve (reverse causality)  
Fix: add manager fixed effects so identification comes from a given manager performing differently across firms; also run specification with firm × calendar-year FE and interacting manager FE (“AKM” style).  

Threat 3 Simultaneous change in other top executives/board (bundle of treatments)  
Fix: control for turnover of CFO, board chair; run sub-samples where only CEO changes.  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R CODE OUTLINE
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
###############################################################
# 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------
###############################################################
library(data.table)    # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)        # high-dimensional FE regressions
library(MatchIt)       # matching
library(ggplot2)

###############################################################
# 1. Data loading --------------------------------------------
###############################################################
dt <- fread("firm_manager_panel_1969_1999.csv")   # each row = firm-year

###############################################################
# 2. Variable construction -----------------------------------
###############################################################
# Identify first fiscal year a manager appears at each firm
setorder(dt, firm_id, fiscal_year)
dt[, new_manager := manager_id != shift(manager_id, type = "lag"), 
      by = firm_id]
dt[, event_time := ifelse(new_manager, 0, NA_integer_)]
dt[, event_time := zoo::na.locf(event_time, na.rm = FALSE), by = firm_id]
dt[, event_time := fiscal_year - first(fiscal_year[event_time == 0]), 
      by = firm_id]

# Treatment dummy: post-arrival years 0,1,2,…
dt[, treat := (event_time >= 0)]

# Restrict to ±5-year window for stacked event study
stack <- dt[event_time >= -5 & event_time <= 5]

###############################################################
# 3. Create matched control firms -----------------------------
###############################################################
# Simple exact match by 3-digit SIC, size decile, calendar year
stack[, size_dec := cut(size_total_assets, 
                        quantile(size_total_assets, probs = seq(0,1,0.1), na.rm=TRUE),
                        include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)]
treated <- unique(stack[new_manager == TRUE, .(firm_id, fiscal_year, sic3, size_dec)])
controls <- stack[!firm_id %in% treated$firm_id]

match.form <- matchit(new_manager ~ size_dec + sic3 + roa_pre, 
                      data = stack, method = "nearest", ratio = 3)
stack <- match.data(match.form)

###############################################################
# 4. Main regression  ----------------------------------------
###############################################################
# Example outcome = log CAPEX / assets
stack[, y := log(1 + capex/assets)]

# Stacked DID with firm and calendar year FE
est1 <- feols(y ~ treat | firm_id + fiscal_year, data = stack,
              cluster = "firm_id")
summary(est1)

# Dynamic event-study
for (k in -5:5) stack[, paste0("leadlag",k) := as.integer(event_time == k)]
event.form <- as.formula(paste("y ~", 
               paste(paste0("leadlag", -4:5), collapse = " + "), 
               "| firm_id + fiscal_year"))
est2 <- feols(event.form, data = stack, cluster = "firm_id")
etable(est2, drop = "Constant")

###############################################################
# 5. Robustness: Manager FE (“AKM” style) ---------------------
###############################################################
est3 <- feols(y ~ 0 | firm_id + manager_id + fiscal_year, data = dt,
              cluster = "firm_id")   # coefficient on manager FE retrieved separately

###############################################################
# 6. Plot event-study coefficients ----------------------------
###############################################################
coef_df <- data.frame(
   tt = -4:5,
   b  = coef(est2)[1:10],
   se = se(est2)[1:10])
ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = tt, y = b)) +
  geom_point() + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = b - 1.96*se, ymax = b + 1.96*se)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() + ylab("Effect on log(CAPEX/assets)") + xlab("Event time")
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. EXPECTED RESULTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Economic priors suggest sizable manager fixed effects. I expect incoming “aggressive” managers to raise investment and leverage by roughly 5–10 ％ of the sample s.d. and to improve ROA by ~0.5 pp (≈ 5 ％ of mean ROA) within three years. Stock-market reactions should be positive on announcement for high-reputation managers (2-3 ％ abnormal return).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. VALIDITY CHECKLIST SELF-ASSESSMENT
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1: No differential pre-trends (tested via event-study) ………………… 0.8  
C2: Exogenous treatment timing (forced vs voluntary) ………………… 0.6  
C3: No spillovers / SUTVA …………………………………………………………… 0.7  
C4: Common support / covariate balance …………………………………… 0.9  
C5: Correct standard-error clustering ………………………………………… 1.0  

Overall average ≈ 0.8 → reasonably credible, but exogeneity remains the weakest link; results should be interpreted as “manager effect conditional on observed move patterns,” not pure random assignment.
